# `Q-1-29` — String Length Constraint Violation

> A string value is shorter or longer than the schema's length
> constraint allows.

## What this means

A schema can require that a string property be at least *N*
characters long, at most *M* characters long, or both. This error
fires when your string falls outside that range.

The terminal message names the actual length and the bound that
was violated — either "less than minimum N" or "greater than
maximum N".

## Why this happens

The pattern usually appears on properties where the schema models
an identifier, abbreviation, or other field with a known shape:

- An empty string in a slot that requires a non-empty value (for
  example, an identifier or short name).
- A field shortened past a minimum because of an editor's
  auto-trim or an upstream pipeline truncating values.
- A field padded past a maximum because of accidental concatenation
  or a value imported from a longer-form source.

## How to fix

Adjust the value to fit the bound named in the error. If the
constraint feels wrong for your case — for example, the schema
demands a length your input legitimately cannot meet — the
property may not be the right slot for the value, or the schema
may need to be relaxed.
